title: TIC quarterly U.S. gross external debt (as-of 2026-09-30) — the only edition of this series that has ever been materially late, twenty days after the CR expires
source: EST: home.treasury.gov/data/treasury-international-capital-tic-system/release-dates-of-tic-data, fetched direct 2026-09-09 (plain curl, HTTP 200, 111,182 bytes) by the tic-quarterly-external-debt-2026-09-30 initial-research adjacency sweep — its 2026 table's December row reads '15 | 15 | 31' across the monthly / quarterly-nonfinancial / gross-external-debt columns. The same page's note block gives the rule: 'The release dates are the last business day of each quarter (March, June, September, and December).' Corroborated mechanically: 2026-12-31 is a Thursday and the last business day of December 2026 (5 U.S.C. 6103 holidays reconstructed from the statute), offset +0 from the page's own rule, which reproduces 56 of 64 dated publications 2011-2026 at +0. Filed estimate per this lane's no-self-confirm limit on an event discovered in-sweep. Checked 2026-09-09
notes: DISCOVERED during the tic-quarterly-external-debt-2026-09-30 initial research (2026-09-09), which found this edition was not in the calendar at all despite being the one that carries this series' entire schedule risk. THE REASON TO TRACK IT: split by release month, the archive's 64 dated publications run September 15/15 at +0, March 15/15, June 19/20 (once three weekend nominal stamps are recognised as stamps rather than delays) — and December 10 of 14. Both of the series' materially late publications are December editions and both are appropriations events: 2019-01-31 at +31, during the 35-day funding lapse of 2018-12-22 to 2019-01-25, and 2026-01-16 at +16, flagged '16 (delayed)' on Treasury's own release-dates page. The other two December exceptions are -1 (published a day early). AND THE MECHANISM IS LIVE: cr-expiry-2026-12-11 falls twenty days before this date. The CR enacted 2026-09-02 as PL 119-103 funds agencies only through 2026-12-11, and government-funding-deadline-2026-09-30's own pulse warns not to inherit its aversion base case into December, because the incentive that produced the September outcome was funding past the midterms. Also note the second, smaller December oddity this session did not resolve: Treasury's gross-external-debt statistics page states December alone releases at 10 AM rather than 4 PM, which the release-dates page's blanket 'All data releases occur at 4 p.m.' contradicts. It publishes the as-of 2026-09-30 position, an as-of Q3 quarter. Impact LOW and symbols empty on the standing grounds: 16:00 ET (or 10:00) is after or before nothing that trades on it, the data is a quarter stale, there is no accompanying press release, and no house playbook is macro-keyed. Proposed as an estimate; nothing here licenses an entry.
